title: OpenWOP deprecation register
description: Shape of spec/v1/deprecations.json — the index of every surface an RFC or spec annotation has deprecated in v1.x (status: deprecated), plus surfaces the v2 program proposes to deprecate but no RFC has yet (status: proposed). In v1.x the register records deprecations; it never creates one (COMPATIBILITY.md §7). It is not a wire artifact and is deliberately kept out of schemas/.

surface.description: The wire-visible name of the thing: a field path, a header, a profile id, a schema file, a prose convention.

deprecatedIn.description: Corpus or suite version, or the RFC that deprecated it. null when status is proposed.

authority.description: The RFC section or spec annotation that made (or, for proposed, would make) the deprecation.

removeIn.description: Protocol major.minor at which the surface is removed. v1.x deprecations remove no earlier than 2.0 (COMPATIBILITY.md §7). A `v2-minor` row (RFC 0197) instead names the 2.x minor at which the v2 surface is removed; `check-removal-dates.mjs` compares it to `spec/v2/release.json` `version` minor-by-minor, not major-by-major.

codemod.description: Identifier of the codemod that rewrites consumers, once one exists (v2 program C.11).

file.description: Repo-relative path that documents the deprecation (or the surface, for proposed rows).

token.description: A literal substring the file must still contain; the gate fails when it drifts.

removalTrigger.description: RFC 0176 §C.2: the event(s) that remove the surface. `v2.0-cut` — absent from the v2 representation from the cut; `v1-end-of-support` — removed from the v1 representation when every INTEROP-MATRIX host has produced a non-vacuous v2 bundle plus 90 days (charter Phase 0 rule). A SET, because §C.2 gives one row two independent removal events: the wrapper, the dotted mirror and Capabilities-Etag are absent from v2 at the cut AND removed from v1 at end-of-support, and a scalar could express only one. Until 2026-09-04 those rows carried `v1-end-of-support` alone while `v2-well-known-one-resource` asserted the `v2.0-cut` obligation by name — the scenario was right about the effect and the data could not say so. A bare string remains valid for rows with one trigger. Optional; removeIn stays the version. `v2-minor` — RFC 0197 §A.2: removed from the v2 representation at `removeIn` (a 2.N minor, inside the major), admitted only when `scripts/check-v2-retirement.mjs` proves predicates R1–R6 for the row. A `v2-minor` row MUST carry `retirement`.

retirement.description: RFC 0197 §A.2 — the machine-readable retirement record. REQUIRED when `removalTrigger` includes `v2-minor`, and meaningless otherwise. `check-v2-retirement.mjs` reads every field: it is the row’s claim about WHAT is being retired, which the gate then falsifies against the committed bundles, the registry census, the declaration and the public history.

class.description: RFC 0197 R4 — the four kinds whose ABSENCE the 2.0 contract already defines. A REQUIRED property, an endpoint, an error code’s meaning and a header are never retirable inside the major.

persistence.description: `advertised`: the schema drops the member at `removeIn` (a family, a facet, an advertised enum value). `persisted`: the member STAYS in the reader schema, annotated `x-openwop-retired-in`, and only emission is forbidden (RFC 0197 §A.3).

family.description: `spec/v2/declaration.json` `families[].key` of the family that ADVERTISES the surface. RFC 0197 R5 reads that row’s `maturity`.

deprecatedInMinor.description: The 2.x minor in which the deprecation row was announced. RFC 0197 R2 requires `removeIn` to be at least two minors later; the 30-day leg is read from the public history, never from this field.

discovery.description: Where the surface would appear in a host’s v2 discovery document. RFC 0197 R3 scans every committed `evidence/v2-host-bundles/*.json` `discovery.document` at this path.

value.description: When present, only this value at `path` (or this member of an array at `path`) counts as carrying the surface; when absent, presence of the path is enough.

manifest.description: Where the surface would appear in a PUBLISHED registry manifest. RFC 0197 R3’s registry leg reads the `registryManifestCensus` that `generate-cross-repo-evidence.mjs` writes for this row id.

value.description: When present, only this value at `path` counts.

allOf.$comment: RFC 0197 §A.2 — a `v2-minor` trigger without a `retirement` record is a claim the gate cannot falsify, so the schema refuses it.
